title: Xanthe and the Oath
premise: Ulyana Zhou, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Veth, has spent his whole life in the valley of Ashmoor, where wards keep magic out — and keep something older locked in. When the wards shatter on the same night the stars go dark, Ulyana is dragged beyond the border by a fugitive girl, Xanthe, who carries a fragment of the god's stolen voice inside a bone charm. Hunted by the Oathbound order that betrayed Veth and by a warlord gathering the godless, Ulyana must choose between restoring his god and freeing the magic that could save or doom the valley. In the end, Ulyana shatters the charm to release Veth's voice to everyone equally — dissolving the old covenant — and finds his belonging not in an oath, but in the ragged family that chose to stay with him.
about_author: Wren Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken oaths in municipal court records before turning to fantasy. They write about people who belong to places that refuse to belong to them, and live in a drafty house full of unsanctioned cats.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine patrol on Ashmoor's border the night the wards fail: the sky goes black, the wardstones crack, and Ulyana's god-mark burns cold for the first time in years. He drags a wounded stranger — Xanthe — out of the collapsing perimeter. Emotional beat: dread and disorientation as the only world he knows begins to break.

chapters.title: What the Valley Kept Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Hidden in Ashmoor's undercity, Xanthe hides the bone charm and lies about who she is, while Ulyana interrogates her and the town's elders argue over sending for the Oathbound. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into reluctant alliance when Oathbound riders arrive at the gate.

chapters.title: The Order of the Broken Word
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Oathbound commander Serah Ives demands the fugitive; Ulyana swears a false oath to buy time, and his god-mark punishes him for it — proof Veth still listens. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering his own order is the enemy, and the first flicker of hope that his god isn't silent after all.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Gray Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ulyana and Xanthe flee north with two unlikely companions: Doss, a disgraced ward-smith, and Brannic, a warlord's deserter. Xanthe reveals the charm holds a fragment of Veth's stolen voice. Emotional beat: found family forming around a campfire, fragile and half-denied.

chapters.title: The Warlord of the Godless
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Captured by Kavrel March, the warlord who stole Veth's voice decades ago, Xanthe bargains for their lives by pretending to serve him — and learns he wants the charm to finish the theft and become a god himself. Emotional beat: terror braided with defiance as she plays a game she can't afford to lose.

chapters.title: Oaths and Their Price
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana bargains with a river-spirit for passage, paying with a memory of his dead sister, and confronts what his oath has cost him. Serah Ives catches up, but hesitates — she suspects the Order's elders orchestrated Veth's silencing. Emotional beat: grief and the first crack of doubt inside the enemy's ranks.

chapters.title: The Hollow Cathedral
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The party reaches the ruined cathedral where Veth's voice was first imprisoned. Xanthe tries to commune with the charm and is nearly unmade by it; Ulyana anchors her with his oath-mark, fusing their fates. Emotional beat: awe and sacrifice — two strangers bound into something like family.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Brannic, revealed as Kavrel's agent, steals the charm and delivers Xanthe to the warlord. Serah arrives — and instead of arresting Ulyana, gives him the Order's secret records proving the elders' crime. Emotional beat: betrayal's bitter taste answered by an enemy choosing justice over obedience.

chapters.title: The War That Almost Was
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At Kavrel's war-camp on the valley's rim, Xanthe is forced to open the charm; Veth's voice begins pouring into Kavrel, and the ancient war teeters on reignition. Ulyana, Doss, and Serah infiltrate the camp. Emotional beat: desperation at the brink, with everything staked on a single impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Oath Unspoken
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the climax, Ulyana shatters the charm rather than let any one being — god, warlord, or order — own Veth's voice again; the voice scatters into all living things, magic returns to the valley freely, and Kavrel's stolen power collapses. Ulyana's oath dissolves, and the family that fought beside him becomes his covenant instead. Emotional beat: release, grief, and hard-won belonging.
